You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the image rendered as a pencil drawing?
node.criteria: Compare corresponding visual content in SOURCE and EDITED. A pencil-drawn rendering requires recognizable sketch-like contours and pencil-like tonal shading in the depicted content; desaturation, grain, or a uniform texture alone does not establish that rendering. Judge whether this treatment extends throughout the image or substantial content remains photographic.
node.binding: Compare SOURCE and EDITED region by region: determine whether the source scene's depicted objects have been rendered with recognizable pencil-like linework and tonal shading, rather than merely receiving a global color or texture treatment. The requested change is to render the image as a pencil drawing.
node.source_quote: Change the image into pencil drawing
node.endpoint: The image is rendered as a pencil drawing.
node.necessity: This is the requested transformation itself; without it, the instruction is not fulfilled.
node.zero_when: No requested pencil-drawing change is visible; unrelated edits do not count.
node.half_when: About half of the image’s visual content has a concrete pencil-drawn treatment, while substantial content remains in its original non-pencil rendering.
node.full_when: The image’s visual content is rendered throughout in a recognizable pencil-drawing style, with pencil-like contours and tonal shading across corresponding regions; natural variation in texture and lighting is allowed, but desaturation or uniform texture alone is insufficient.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image is substantially desaturated and has a fine grainy texture, but most objects retain soft photographic shading rather than recognizable pencil-drawn contours and tonal hatching. Some edges and surface details look sketch-like, yet the pencil treatment is weak and inconsistent across the scene, so the requested rendering is only partially achieved.
